modern: To the jaundiced honey tastes bitter, and to those bitten by mad dogs water causes fear; and to little children the ball is a fine thing. Why then am I angry? Do you think that a false opinion has less power than the bile in the jaundiced or the poison in someone bitten by a mad dog?

explained.summary: To someone with jaundice, honey tastes bitter; to someone with rabies, water is frightening; to small children a ball is a treasure. So why get angry at people? A false belief distorts how someone sees things just as powerfully as illness does. They aren’t choosing to see wrongly any more than a sick person chooses bitterness.
explained.today: When a friend who’s been badly hurt reads every message as a slight, or someone deep in a conspiracy theory dismisses everything you say, anger won’t help. They’re seeing through a kind of fever, and patience makes more sense.
